target: Z Root Mean Squared (Z-axis RMS acceleration, chosen axis)

risk.description: P(RMS_Z > 0.1028 g) at 3300 RPM without action, held-out experiment M0.0_U20.4_A1B0, posterior after 75% of the speed sweep; limit = P99 of healthy Z RMS

decision.description: Expected-cost-per-hour optimum over speed setpoint (300-3300 RPM, 150 step) and rebalance option, M0.0_U20.4_A1B0, 75% posterior; action=rebalance, derate factor=0.68; costs are assumptions

limitations: Target is the Z-axis RMS (chosen by a documented criterion); X and Y are dominated by the healthy baseline and carry weak unbalance information. The axis choice uses all Mis=0 unbalance rows and the Normal reference.
The data have no time axis: no wear/degradation trajectory, so there is no RUL; the decision is a speed/rebalance choice at a fixed unbalance state.
Misalignment is not modelled physically; the Jeffcott physics only describes the unbalance-induced response. Misalignment-only groups are predicted by the healthy floor in Pure Physics.

Rotor mass m and eccentricity e are not separately identifiable from RMS vs RPM: the response depends only on k/m, c/m and e/m. m is fixed to 3 kg in least squares; the posterior of m stays close to its prior.
The sensor gain and the physical unbalance radius are absorbed into e; RMS is assumed to be in g. No sensor calibration was available.
Both-disc configurations (TypeA=TypeB=1) are modelled as twice the unbalance mass in phase; phase between the two discs is not modelled.
The healthy-machine background floor (per-RPM mean of the Normal rows) is added in quadrature. It is always kept in training, so the Normal group is not a held-out test set.
Calibration uses one held-out experiment (group M0.0_U20.4, TypeA only). Coverage is measured on only 8 unused RPM points, so the coverage estimate is coarse.

Severity limit = P99 of healthy Z-RMS (a percentile assumption, no ISO limit for raw g units). Decision costs (V_full, C_fail, h_fail, C_rb, H_amort) are assumptions, not data; a sensitivity over C_fail is reported.
Physics is closed-form. The GP surrogate is therefore slower than direct evaluation (speedup_x < 1); no speedup claim is made.

The 5 repeats per (condition, Position, RPM) cell are treated as repeated segments and stay in the same fold; some conditions miss positions for some RPMs (see partial_conditions), so position averaging is unbalanced.
Dataset is recorded bench data according to the user; features are not checked against a second acquisition chain.
